content.title: Oregon Ducks’ defense stifles Virginia Tech in 1st-round NCAA Tournament victory
content.text: Oregon DucksUpdated: Mar. 21, 2026, 12:02 a.m.Published: Mar. 20, 2026, 12:51 p.m.Virginia Tech guard Samyha Suffren (12) drives past Oregon guard Katie Fiso (2) during a first round game of the 2026 NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament held at the Moody Center on March 20, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Scott Wachter/NCAA Photos via Getty Images)NCAA Photos via Getty ImagesBy Aaron Fentress | The Oregonian/OregonLiveAUSTIN, Texas – Oregon coach Kelly Graves entered the NCAA Tournament Friday confident his relatively young team could succeed, but he also wondered how they would respond to the setting and Virginia Tech’s aggressive style of play.Most of Graves’ team, including Katie Fiso and Ehis Etute, weren’t major contributors to last year’s squad that won a first-round matchup with Vanderbilt before falling to Duke.Ultimately, Graves’ confidence proved more warranted than any misgivings.The Ducks built a double-digit lead in the first quarter, weathered a Virginia Tech run in the second, then blew the game open in the third and cruised to a 70-60 women’s basketball win at Moody Center.The Ducks led 67-46 in the fourth quarter before the Hokies closed with a flurry to make the score more respectable.Graves emphasized Thursday that Oregon had to withstand Virginia Tech’s transition offense and remain disciplined against the Hokies’ defense, one of the best in the ACC.Eighth-seeded Oregon (23-12) did all of the above and more. The Ducks shot 48.2% from the field and committed just 13 turnovers. Oregon limited the ninth-seeded Hokies (23-10) to 31.8% shooting.Virginia Tech guard Samyha Suffren (12) is defended by Oregon forward Sarah Rambus and guard Katie Fiso (2) during a first round game of the 2026 NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament held at the Moody Center on March 20, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Scott Wachter/NCAA Photos via Getty Images)NCAA Photos via Getty ImagesOregon used a few big runs to put the Hokies on their heels. A 12-0 run in the first quarter helped the Ducks to a 22-11 lead. Virginia Tech rallied to trail 39-35 after scoring the first basket of the third quarter. Next came a 17-0 Oregon run that put the Ducks up 53-31 with 3:26 remaining.Any chance of a Virginia Tech comeback all but evaporated when Oregon opened the final quarter with a 6-0 run to lead 61-40 with 8:03 remaining.TOP PERFORMERSFiso led the Ducks with 22 points on 9-of-12 shooting and committed just one turnover to go along with four assists.Etute didn’t shoot well, going 4 of 12, but contributed 11 points and 11 rebounds. Mia Jacobs scored 13 points, going 3 for 4 from three-point range.Oregon outscored the Hokies 34-16 in the paint. “We really felt we had an advantage inside,” Oregon coach Kelly Graves said. Helping that effort were reserve forwards Amina Muhammad, who scored seven points, and Sarah Rambus, who added eight. “I thought our bench, particularly in the first half, was really strong for us,” Graves said.The Hokies received 21 points from Carys Baker, but the other four starters combined to make just 6 of 32 shots for 22 points.FIRST QUARTER TONE SETTERThe Ducks began the game doing exactly what Graves hoped they wouldn’t. They turned the ball over four times early, allowing Virginia Tech to get its fast-paced offense going.As a result, the Ducks trailed 9-7 just short of four minutes into the quarter. From that point on, Oregon dominated the quarter.Then came the Ducks’ 12-0 run that put them up 19-9. Oregon ended the quarter leading 22-11 after shooting 71.4% from the field.The Hokies, a mediocre shooting team, went 4-for-18 from the field and made just one of five 3-point attempts.NEXT UPThe Ducks play top-seeded Texas (35-3) in Sunday’s second round at 3 p.m. The Longhorns won 87-45 over Missouri State (23-13) in Saturday’s second game at Moody Center.
